title: I used AI heavily while developing this small online idle/base-building game. Now looking for balancing feedback
author: Epceon
selftext:
I made a small online game called Cidle Online. It’s an idle base-building game with PvP aspects, playable directly in browser on both mobile and desktop.

A lot of the development process was AI-assisted, especially for rapid iteration, UI/workflow ideas and implementing systems faster as a solo developer.

Playable instantly here:  
[gament.no/cidle](http://gament.no/cidle)

I’m currently trying to improve balancing/progression and would really appreciate some honest feedback from a few players.

Feedback can be given ingame through:  
Settings > Feedback

Or directly on this post of course.

comments.author: Intelligent-Gap494
comments.body: I honestly did not understand what the game is about, is it multiplayer game?

replies.author: Epceon
replies.body: It is a multiplayer idle base building game. The main goal is to build up bases and climb the highscores. You can see live all players if they are online and what jobs they are doing, raid others or gift them chests.

replies.author: Intelligent-Gap494
replies.body: I have tried it, the concept sounds good, but seems to unpolished, does not have a clear identity, and also not in love with the graphics, maybe try to settle on a specific style, does not need to look awsome , just consistent.

replies.author: Epceon
replies.body: Thanks for trying it and the feedback. Where did we lose you and was the onboarding clear? I can agree with the graphics, but I have tried to keep it consistent - do you have any examples of whats stands out?

replies.author: Intelligent-Gap494
replies.body: What stood out to me instantly was that onboarding was basically telling me to use speed ups all the time, that scream heavy-monetization, kinda lost me already there.

replies.author: Epceon
replies.body: Thats a very good point, thank you.
